results.evidence: The contradiction is real: gain_ft/loss_ft (6,550/1,820) are one party's Day-1 figures for road to a camp beyond the summit, while the itinerary, totalNote and approach prose say 5,600/5,600 round trip. The only detailed ascent record (Abegg, Aug 2012) confirms +6,550/-1,820/6.3 mi for road to summit to camp, and it implies roughly 1,000+ ft of intermediate loss before the summit. That means a true car-to-car gain is likely well ABOVE 5,600 ft (5,570 ft is only the net rise from 850 ft to 6,420 ft), so neither stored figure could be confirmed as the round-trip total. No second independent source gives a round-trip total, so nothing was patched. loss_ft 1,820 is clearly a one-way partial figure, but I found no sourced replacement.

results.fact: Elevation of the high camp above Berdeen Lake
results.evidence: Berdeen Lake is at 5,016 ft (Wikipedia/WDFW high-lakes listing), so the bivy entry's elevation is correct for the lake itself. The only ascent record says the party 'descended about 500 ft' from the 6,400-ft summit to a camp 'about 800 ft above Berdeen Lake', i.e. about 5,800-5,900 ft, which supports the 5,800 waypoint. However, the bivy entry is titled lake 'benches' and its capacity text describes spots above the shore, which could be a separate lake-level camp. I found only one source for the higher camp's elevation, so nothing was patched.

results.fact: Day-1 gain to the Berdeen Lake camp stated in the bivy entry
results.evidence: The 'Berdeen Lake benches' bivy notes call the road-to-camp day 'a very big first day with four thousand feet of gain', but the net rise alone from the 850-ft road end to a camp near 5,800 ft is about 4,950 ft. The only ascent record gives +6,550 ft for that day, and the row's waypoint note repeats 6,550 ft. With only one external source, nothing was patched.

Wikipedia confirms that Fred and Helmy Beckey made the peak's first ascent in 1940. The 1964 AAJ note on the 1963 Northern Pickets outing shows that the fa field's party (Ardussi, Magnusson, Mech, Swanson, July 31, 1963) made a NEW ROUTE on the east face: a diagonal gully and chimney (class 5) to the first notch north of the summit, then the ridge and ledges. So fa is a route FA, not the peak's FA. It is not established whether that 1963 line is the same as this row's NW-couloir/north-ridge/headwall line, and no second source ties either party to this exact route, so nothing was patched. fa and the beta sentence 'This classic Beckey-era first ascent' need an owner decision on route identity.

The detailed 2016 ascent report grades the crux headwall crack 'either Class 5.8+ or 5.2/A1, depending on the method of attack'. Four rendered fields on the row agree (grade, rock_grade, aid_grade, descent_text, plus the summit waypoint's own directions). The summit waypoint note's '5.6' is the outlier, and the partner-requirements skill line repeats it. I found no second independent grading of this line.

results.correct_value: roughly 46-50 mi round trip from the Hannegan Trailhead
results.evidence: The '54 miles' comes from a 2016 party's whole-trip total (54 mi; 18,600 ft), and that trip also climbed Phantom Peak and West Challenger Peak, so it is not this route alone. A 2015 party reaching the same objective area by the Big Beaver/Wiley Ridge approach logged 45 miles for 8 days. The row's own figures agree on the high-40s: itinerary days sum to 46.5 mi, totalNote says 48-50 mi, the summit waypoint is at 22.5 mi one way, and dist_km 37.4 (~23.2 mi one way) is a consistent one-way figure. The trail to Whatcom Pass is about 17 mi one way. The beta's 54 mi and the road note's '50+ mile' are the outliers. dist_km is left untouched.

results.fact: Crooked Thumb Glacier moraine camp elevation
results.evidence: The 2016 ascent report gives no elevation for the lateral-moraine camp. Its only 7,800-ft figure is the forced BIVOUAC ledge on Crooked Thumb's north ridge ('Bivouac Site: North Ridge of Crooked Thumb Peak (Elev. 7800 feet)'). That suggests the campsite waypoint's 7,800 was taken from the bivouac, not the camp. The row's itinerary is also internally inconsistent: day 2 puts camp near 7,700 ft, while day 3 (+2,200/-300 to the 8,129-ft summit) implies about 6,200 ft. I found no topo or second source for the moraine camp, so nothing was patched.

The contradiction is real (header 'Mar-May' against best_season/seasonal_guidance centred on late July-September). But every dated ascent I found is a snow-season climb: Steven Song, April 2026 on the SW Face (with the ski-pioneered SW Face route); Brisbine, May 30, 2009; onehikeaweek, June 4, 2016; cascadeclimbers, June 3, 2017; nwhikers, May 9, 2009; and a winter guided ascent. I found no dated summer (Jul-Sep) ascent, so the summer window in best_season/seasonal_guidance is unsupported. Mar-May also omits the documented early-June ascents. There were not enough sources to set a window, so nothing was patched.

results.correct_value: about 6,200 ft car to car (gain and loss)
results.evidence: One trip report records 6.2 mi round trip and 5,955 ft of gain from 1,096 ft to 7,051 ft ('6000 ft in three miles'). The source of the 7,400 figure (Brisbine, May 2009: '10 miles; 7400 feet gained & lost') says the party 'accumulated an extra 1000 feet' on a failed East Ridge detour, so the standard line is about 6,400 ft by that account. Two independent sources agree on roughly 6,000-6,400 ft. That matches the itinerary's 6,200 gain and 6,200 loss, so gain_ft and loss_ft (an out-and-back must be equal) are set to the itinerary total.

results.fact: Where the route's Class 4 moves occur
results.evidence: Both placements are documented, on different parts and variants of the route. The April 2026 SW Face party carried a rope 'mostly for the forested bluffs' low on the route and found them 'class 3 with maybe a few class 4 moves', which supports rock_grade. The South Buttress line's crux is the 'slime-coated rock slabs near the top' (Brisbine 2009; the 2026 report also notes the wet slabs above the 3rd-class chimney), which supports pitch_detail and beta. Beta labels these as two variants that converge near the summit.

The row conflates TWO different routes. The 1988 AAJ note records Bryan Burdo and Andy Cairns's North Face route (IV 5.10): four pitches up the central chimney, three on an exposed rib, then monstrous chockstones. That is what overview, beta, pitch_detail, pitches and gain_ft describe, and the note calls the chimney 'probably the melted-out version of the 1974 Kloke-Simon route'. The Northwest Mountaineering Journal's 2005 winter report (Ade Miller and Stuart Taylor, March 13, 2005) is of the Northeast Face Couloir, which it credits as 'Kloke-Simon, July 1976'. That report is what fa, rappels, itinerary, descent, detailed_rack, turnaround and bail describe. Each FA is correct for its own route, and the Kloke-Simon year differs between sources (1974 vs 1976; another snippet gives 1972). Fixing this needs an owner decision on which route this row is (or a split), not a text patch.

This is the same two-route conflation. The Burdo-Cairns North Face route described by overview/beta/pitch_detail is graded IV 5.10 by the 1988 AAJ note, so '5.6' would be wrong for it. The Kloke-Simon Northeast Face Couloir described by the rest of the row has a lower rock band the 2005 party called 'mid-fifth in summer', which is consistent with a 5.6-range grade. Which grade is right depends on which route the row is meant to be. Only one source grades each route, so nothing was patched.
